record.paper_title: Recent results and open problems on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities
record.context_brief: Whether the blowup set can be only infinity in R^N
record.original_question: Let q ≥ p and Ω = R^N. For an unbounded solution, define the blowup set E = { x_0 ∈ R^N ∪ {∞} : there exist x_n → x_0 and t_n → T^* with u(t_n,x_n) → ∞ }. Theorem 3.7 states that in R^N either E = R^N ∪ {∞} or E = {∞}. Theorem 3.6 provides examples of the first alternative, where the solution diverges at every spatial point as t → ∞. Does there also exist initial data for which the second alternative occurs, namely E = {∞}, so that the solution becomes unbounded only by escaping to spatial infinity and not at any finite spatial point?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.7 Assume q ≥ p and Ω ⊂ R^N (unbounded). Assume that φ is such that u is unbounded, with either T∗ < ∞ or T∗ = ∞. (ii) If Ω = R^N, then either E = R^N ∪ {∞} or E = {∞}.
Open problem 9. Does there exist φ such that E = {∞} when q ≥ p and Ω = R^N ? Theorem 3.6 provides some φ such that Ω = R^N and E = R^N ∪ {∞}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Cauchy problem on the whole Euclidean space:
  u_t - Δu = u^p - |∇u|^q,    (t,x) ∈ (0,T*) × R^N,
  u(0,x) = φ(x),               x ∈ R^N,
where p > 1, q ≥ p, and φ ≥ 0 is a sufficiently smooth, bounded initial datum. Let u be the (classical) maximal solution defined on the maximal existence interval [0,T*), with T* ∈ (0, ∞]. Assume that u is unbounded, i.e. limsup_{t → T*^-} ‖u(t,·)‖_{L^∞(R^N)} = ∞.

Define the (extended) blow-up set
  E := { x_0 ∈ R^N ∪ {∞} : there exist sequences x_n → x_0 in R^N ∪ {∞} and t_n → T*^- with u(t_n, x_n) → ∞ }.

It is known that under these hypotheses one has the dichotomy E = R^N ∪ {∞} or E = {∞}, and that the first alternative E = R^N ∪ {∞} is realized by some choices of φ (with T* = ∞, the solution diverging at every spatial point as t → ∞).

Question: Does there exist an initial datum φ for which the second alternative occurs, namely E = {∞}? Equivalently, is there a choice of φ such that the corresponding solution u becomes unbounded only by escaping to spatial infinity, while remaining locally bounded in space-time on every compact subset of R^N × [0,T*)?
artifact.category_tag: Blow-up for parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in the recent survey on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities. A web search did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving the existence of an initial datum on R^N (with q ≥ p) for which the blow-up set is exactly {∞}; related literature (Souplet and coauthors, Quittner–Souplet monograph) discusses the dichotomy and examples of E = R^N ∪ {∞}, but not a construction or refutation of the E = {∞} case.

status_evidence.title: Superlinear Parabolic Problems: Blow-up, Global Existence and Steady States
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph treating blow-up phenomena for parabolic problems including gradient nonlinearities; standard reference establishing the dichotomy framework but not resolving the E={∞} case on R^N.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference for the framework; does not contain a resolution of the question.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of global solutions for nonlinear parabolic equations involving gradient blow-up phenomena (Rodriguez-Bernal, Souplet)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies global behavior and gradient blow-up; discusses related dichotomies but on bounded domains and does not address E={∞} on R^N.
status_evidence.claim: Related results do not settle the open question on R^N.

status_evidence.title: Publications of Philippe Souplet
status_evidence.snippet: List of publications on parabolic problems with gradient nonlinearities; no listed work resolving this specific question.
status_evidence.claim: No subsequent resolution found in the author's publication list.
